summary: Round 6, doc-only again. NO ASSERTION WAS WEAKENED: the only change under format/src/test is SubscriptionEventGrantTest's class javadoc plus one .as() message string; every predicate is byte-identical, and .contains("byteStart=4096")/.contains("byteLen=65536") at :285-286 are untouched. THE NEW JAVADOC CLAIM CHECKS OUT BY READING: forcing decode to return RANGE_ABSENT reds exactly three cases -- aV3EventSurvivesAROUNDTrip:57-58 (two of its three fixtures carry a range), aRangeStartingAtBYTEZEROIsNotMistakenForABSENT:81-82, and GoldenSubscriptionEventTest:91's decode of v3DirectWithRange. toStringCarriesTheGrantsEXPIRY... is NOT one of them, because it constructs directly, so 'three' is right rather than four. TREE CLAIMS I CHECKED AND FOUND TRUE: 0 presigning backends (every presign is in src/test), client's only production dependency is api(project(":format")), the client package is exactly the five types named, SegmentWriter:109 writes CODEC_NONE unconditionally, SegmentReader never mentions codecAndFlags at all, SegmentPublisher.headerRangeEndInclusive:147 exists and SegmentPublisherTest:145 calls it, SegmentKey.headerLenOf and SegmentFormat.PREAMBLE_BYTES are both public in format, the golden pair really is 128 and 123 bytes, and there really are six subscription-event golden files. ON THE ASSIGNED QUESTION -- DECISION (b)'s NARROWED JUSTIFICATION IS TRUE: with the coordinates the union slice GET can be issued concurrently with the header range; without them the directory must be parsed first, so the two are strictly sequential. Each run block is length-prefixed and CRC32C'd by SegmentWriter.encodeRun, so a concurrently-fetched slice is self-validating and the concurrency is real rather than nominal. One round trip is genuinely what they buy. ON THE FIFTH WORDING OF CRITERION 2: it does NOT hold, and both breaks are downstream of that same true claim. First, the one round trip is the one property criterion 2 does not assert -- it asserts bytes and requests, and those are IDENTICAL whether the reader reads byteStart from the event or from RunEntry, so the clause that would earn the fields is stated and not made falsifiable. Second, the union clause added this round moved the crossover above the ~400 share the same criterion mandates whole-object at, and the per-byte price that decides it is pinned by nothing in the tree. Details in the two findings. One minor: three files match the sweep table's own named patterns and have no row; all three are benign, so it is a completeness point about an artifact that declares itself THE enumeration, not a correction.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'AND a consumer that uses the event's coordinates to drive it' against 'the assertion is on BYTES FETCHED AND ON REQUESTS MADE, BOTH'), with ADR-0044:114-118 and SubscriptionEvent.java:120-123
findings.title: The one round trip is the whole of decision (b) and is the one thing criterion 2 does not assert: bytes and requests are identical whether the slice extents come from the event or from RunEntry, so a sequential reader using the DIRECTORY's coordinates passes every clause and buys nothing
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION, inside the intended implementation: in the bounded reader, delete the use of event.byteStart()/event.byteLen() and substitute reader.find(event.key()).byteStart()/byteLen() from the directory it has just fetched -- i.e. fetch the header range, AWAIT it, parse the directory, compute the union from RunEntry, then issue the slice. Walk criterion 2. Requests: still exactly two at every K, the header range and one union slice, so the K=1, K=crossover and K=crossover+1 cases all report 2. Bytes: byte-for-byte identical, because RunEntry carries the same extents the event does -- ADR-0044:106-112 says so itself. Codec: the directory was fetched, the non-CODEC_NONE flag is read and refused. Criterion 1's derived threshold: untouched. Criteria 3 and 4: untouched. NOTHING REDS. The mutation violates only the words 'a consumer that uses the event's coordinates to drive it', and that clause has no assertion form anywhere in the row -- the row says the assertion is on bytes and requests, and those are exactly the two quantities that cannot see it. This is the row's own ASSERTED-NOT-STATED distinction, which M5.45g's criterion 5 makes explicitly and M5.66's criterion 2 does not make here. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE ONE THE ROW WAS CREATED TO PREVENT. ADR-0044:114-118 keeps the fields on exactly one ground -- 'What actually survives is one round trip, and that is the whole of it' -- and :124-127 hands M5.66 the question 'is one round trip on the direct path worth 5.4%?'. A row whose criteria cannot distinguish a reader that saves the round trip from one that does not cannot answer that question. Its owner discharges criterion 2 with a sequential reader, then criterion 3 'corrects' SubscriptionEvent.java:111 to say a reader consumes them, and the field looks earned having bought zero round trips -- which is verbatim the outcome criterion 2 already names as a defect two clauses earlier, for the whole-object case. THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE AND IT COSTS NOTHING EXTRA, because the cases criterion 2 already demands are the ones to assert it in: the slice request is issued BEFORE the header response is delivered. That is directly observable at the same seam the row already counts at -- a fake that withholds the header response and asserts the slice request has already arrived reds a sequential reader and greens a concurrent one. Note that a wrong-coordinates fixture is NOT a sufficient substitute: it pins that the event's numbers are read, but a reader that reads them and still waits for the header saves nothing, and saving is the entire justification.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 1, 'the crossover is MEASURED ... the code's threshold is DERIVED from the recorded number' and 'CostTable HOLDS NO PER-BYTE PRICE ... the bandwidth half comes from somewhere this row must name') against criterion 2 ('at ADR-0042's ~400-of-1,600 node share the bounded path must NOT be taken at all')
findings.title: The union clause added this round moves the crossover ABOVE the ~400 share at which criterion 2 mandates whole-object -- ~1,556 on the row's own cited R12 price -- so criteria 1 and 2 are now mutually unsatisfiable, and the per-byte price that decides which way they break is pinned by nothing in the tree
findings.failure_scenario: ARITHMETIC, on the only price the row cites -- research R12, docs/research/00-problem/02-cost-model.md:299, one GET == 19.5 KiB at $0.02/GB. Last round the bounded path was 1+K requests, which put the crossover at ~331, BELOW 400, so criterion 2's ~400 clause was consistent. This round's clause fixes the bounded path at TWO requests at every K, so the extra cost is ONE GET regardless of K and the bandwidth saved is (8 MiB - header - union). With the union tight (see the second arm) that is 8,192 - 78 - 5.2K KiB, and the bounded path wins while that exceeds 19.5 KiB, i.e. up to K ~= 1,556. So an honest measurement records ~1,556, criterion 1 requires the code's threshold to be DERIVED from it, and at K = 400 the derived branch takes the BOUNDED path -- which criterion 2 forbids in the same sentence: 'exactly the whole-object GET, one request, no more bytes'. The K~400 case reds the intended implementation. This is the failure the row names one clause later and asks not to repeat: 'A criterion that reds the intended implementation is worse than a loose one, because it looks strict.' AND THE ESCAPE IS WORSE THAN THE CONTRADICTION, because the price is free. I confirmed the row's own premise: nothing in the tree holds a per-byte price -- no perGb, no egress, no per-byte figure in cost.md, which prices requests only -- so the owner names the bandwidth price and the crossover follows it. Name in-region S3 GET egress, which is genuinely $0, and the crossover is 0: the bounded path is never taken at any K, K=crossover and K=crossover+1 are K=0 and K=1, and the row's second arm (take the fields off the wire) is selected by a price nobody argued rather than by the round-trip question ADR-0044:124-127 created it to answer. Name anything between, and the boundary cases land wherever the owner needs them to. The measurement binds nothing -- the same defect criterion 1's 'DERIVED, not merely compared' clause exists for, displaced one level up into the input. SECOND ARM, WHICH IS THE SAME QUANTITY: criterion 2 requires 'ONE UNION SLICE' and bounds bytes at 'the header range plus the sum of byteLen plus a stated constant', but nothing constrains WHERE the K runs sit in the segment, and the gap between those two quantities is exactly the union's waste. SegmentWriter:31 sorts by (indexId, partitionId) and its javadoc claims contiguity for 'one consumer' -- but a RunKey is one (index, partition) and the K of this criterion is a NODE's share across many indices, so a node's runs are contiguous within each index and interleaved across them. A fixture whose K runs are consecutive directory entries makes the union exactly sum(byteLen), constant 0, and greens the byte bound at all three K. In production the same implementation unions min(byteStart) to max(byteStart+byteLen) across interleaved indices and fetches most of the 8 MiB in TWO requests where whole-object fetches it in ONE -- strictly worse on both axes, every assertion green. It is the shape the row warns about in its own State cell ('discharges criterion 2 against a local harness production does not use'). Both arms need the same two sentences: pin the bandwidth price the crossover is computed from (or drop the ~400 mandate and let the derived threshold stand alone, since the two cannot both be free), and require the K runs in the fixture to be INTERLEAVED as production writes them, so the stated constant has to cover real union waste rather than a fixture's.

findings.title: Three files match the table's own named patterns and have no row, in a table that declares itself THE enumeration -- all three are benign, so this is completeness, not a correction
findings.failure_scenario: The table at :315-316 names its patterns (byteStart, byteLen, coordinates, byte range, M5.44, ADR-0043, VERSION_3) and :341-346 declares itself the single enumeration, which M5.66's criterion 3 then points at instead of copying -- the rung-4 move, and the right one. Grepping those patterns over *.java and *.md, excluding review/ and backlog.md, returns three files with no row: format/src/main/java/binjava/format/Grant.java:7 ('ADR-0041, M5.44'), ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/SegmentProxy.java:387 ('the defect M5.44's row records'), ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/SubscriptionHub.java:494 ('the reason ADR-0043 records'). I read all three and NONE asserts the coordinates earn their place, so no correction is owed and M5.66's owner would lose nothing by not seeing them -- which is why this is minor and not the round-1 and round-2 shape, where the missing rows carried live retired claims. It is worth one line each only because the table already carries rows of exactly this benign class for the same reason it gives at :330: 'Listed because the artifact is only worth what its enumeration is.' Two files matching the patterns are listed as 'Confirmed, nothing to correct' and three are absent; the rule the table states for itself does not distinguish them. Recording this in the commit body is a sufficient answer.
